summary: The United States launched a major new wave of strikes against Iranian military targets, including first-time use of unmanned suicide vessels, while Iran fired missiles from Bandar Abbas toward the Strait of Hormuz and the Konarak naval base was hit. The U.S. declared a blockade of all Iranian ports and announced it would manage the Strait of Hormuz as 'Guardian of Hormuz' with a 20% transit fee. Simultaneously, Houthi forces in Yemen intensified ballistic missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, prompting airport closures, and Israel conducted an airstrike in Gaza killing a Hamas weapons smuggler while artillery struck southern Lebanon.
key_points: U.S. Central Command conducted a new wave of strikes on 21 Tir targeting Iranian air defenses, coastal radars, missile and drone capabilities, and small boats using fighter jets, naval vessels, and one-way attack drones for the first time. (Source: @shin_persian/7780)

Iran launched at least four missiles from the Chamran base toward the Persian Gulf early Monday 22 Tir, with multiple explosions reported in Bandar Abbas at 5:48, 5:51, 5:53, and 5:55, and the Konarak naval base was hit by four projectiles. (Source: @mamlekate/103876, @rodast_omiddana/75958)

The U.S. Navy announced a blockade of all Iranian ports effective tomorrow at 20:00 GMT, while President Trump declared the U.S. would manage the Strait of Hormuz as 'Guardian of Hormuz' and impose a 20% fee on all cargo transiting the strait. (Source: @SharghDaily/171721, @lelotsenzura/93547)

Houthi forces in Yemen launched ballistic missiles at Saudi Arabia, targeting Abha International Airport and other locations, prompting Saudi air defenses to intercept and Saudi-affiliated authorities to close all airports indefinitely. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/4929, @naya_foriraq/82782, @naya_foriraq/82753)

The Israeli military killed Palestinian weapons smuggler Mustafa Owaisi in an airstrike in southern Gaza, stating he attempted to smuggle military equipment for Hamas's naval and aerial capabilities in violation of the ceasefire. (Source: @manniefabian/58782)

Israeli artillery shelled Kfar Tibnit in southern Lebanon, and residents in the Western Galilee reported loud explosions confirmed by the IDF as strikes deep inside Lebanon. (Source: @redlinkleb/31172, @N12chat/217246)

The IDF's Givati Brigade concluded five months of intensive operations in Lebanon, including crossing the Litani River, a significant engagement in Bint Jbeil, and advancing beyond Beaufort Castle. (Source: @idf_telegram/24617)

Iran's Hormozgan province closed all government offices, banks, schools, and universities for two days due to extreme heat, amid ongoing U.S. strikes on the coastal province since 17 Tir. (Source: @VahidOnline/77005)

sections.executive_summary: The United States executed a significant escalation against Iran with a multi-domain strike wave employing unmanned suicide vessels for the first time, targeting air defense systems, coastal radar sites, missile and drone capabilities, and small boats across multiple Iranian locations. Iran responded with missile launches from Bandar Abbas toward the Strait of Hormuz and the Konarak naval base, while the U.S. declared a comprehensive blockade of Iranian ports and asserted control over the Strait of Hormuz under a 'Guardian of Hormuz' framework with a 20% transit levy. Concurrently, Houthi ballistic missile attacks on Saudi Arabia triggered airport closures, and Israel maintained pressure on Hamas in Gaza and Hezbollah in Lebanon through targeted strikes and artillery fire.

points: Iran's Chamran base launched at least four missiles toward the Persian Gulf at 05:20 local time on Monday 22 Tir (July 13), with residents in Bandar Abbas reporting four distinct explosions at 05:48, 05:51, 05:53, and 05:55, the last described as very severe, while Iranian state television denied any explosions occurred in Bandar Abbas or southern areas. (Source: @mamlekate/103876, @rasedal3ado138e/377020)

The Konarak naval base was struck by four projectiles according to local reports, and additional launches from Bandar Abbas toward the Strait of Hormuz were noted, indicating active Iranian missile operations amid U.S. strikes. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/75958, @rasedal3ado138e/377017)

U.S. Central Command confirmed a new wave of offensive strikes on 21 Tir (July 12) hitting dozens of targets in several locations, specifically Iranian military air defense systems, coastal radar sites, missile and drone capabilities, and small boats, utilizing fighter jets, naval vessels, one-way attack drones, and maritime one-way attack drones for the first time. (Source: @shin_persian/7780)

CENTCOM released footage showing unmanned surface vessels (USVs) destroying a submarine and ship maintenance facility, marking the first operational use of such 'naval suicide drones' against Iran. (Source: @yediotnews25/132611, @asafroz/51382)

Hormozgan province authorities ordered the closure of all government offices, banks, educational centers, and universities for Tuesday 23 and Wednesday 24 Tir due to extreme heat, while acknowledging U.S. extensive attacks on various cities in the coastal province since 17 Tir. (Source: @VahidOnline/77005)
President Trump stated that Supreme Leader Khamenei has been 'erased' and his son '90% erased,' signaling a maximalist rhetorical posture toward Iranian leadership. (Source: @inon_yttach/9421)

The IDF announced the killing of Palestinian weapons smuggler Mustafa Owaisi in an airstrike in southern Gaza, stating he attempted to smuggle military equipment for Hamas's naval and aerial capabilities in violation of the ceasefire agreement. (Source: @manniefabian/58782)

Israeli artillery conducted shelling on Kfar Tibnit in southern Lebanon, with the IDF confirming to residents in the Western Galilee that loud explosions heard were from Israeli strikes deep inside Lebanon. (Source: @redlinkleb/31172, @redlinkleb/31211, @N12chat/217246)

The Givati Brigade's reconnaissance company commander summarized five months of intensive operations in Lebanon during 2026, including crossing the Litani River, a significant engagement in Bint Jbeil, and advancing beyond Beaufort Castle, describing the operational employment as beginning before Operation 'Roar of the Lion.' (Source: @idf_telegram/24617)

Israel remains 'out of the picture' in the current U.S.-Iran escalation according to Israeli security sources, while domestic political tensions persist over the Basic Law: Torah Study passed by the Knesset 63-52, drawing criticism from opposition leaders and the IDF Chief of Staff who warned of a 'deep rift' with serving soldiers. (Source: @almogboker78/17705, @inon_yttach/9428, @N12chat/217249)

Israeli airstrike in southern Gaza killed Mustafa Owaisi, identified as a weapons smuggler who attempted to bring military equipment into Gaza for Hamas's naval and aerial wings, with the IDF stating he continued smuggling attempts in recent months violating the ceasefire. (Source: @manniefabian/58782)
No other specific Gaza or West Bank operations were detailed in the provided messages beyond this targeted strike.
Israeli artillery shelled Kfar Tibnit (#كفرتبنيت) in southern Lebanon, with the IDF map marking the location under active shelling. (Source: @redlinkleb/31172, @redlinkleb/31211)
Residents across the Western Galilee reported powerful explosions; the IDF confirmed these were Israeli forces striking targets deep inside Lebanon. (Source: @N12chat/217246)

The Givati Brigade concluded five months of intensive cross-border operations, including crossing the Litani River, a significant clash in Bint Jbeil, and advancing beyond Beaufort Castle, with the battalion commander noting the campaign began before the official start of Operation 'Roar of the Lion.' (Source: @idf_telegram/24617)

Iran reportedly launched missiles and drones at U.S. bases in Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait in response to U.S. strikes, according to Israeli security sources, though no independent confirmation from Syrian or Iraqi sources appears in the messages. (Source: @almogboker78/17705)

Mahan Air flight diverted to Hodeidah airport in Yemen after Sanaa airport was targeted, indicating Iranian aviation assets operating in the Red Sea corridor under threat. (Source: @shin_persian/7776)
The U.S. Navy declared a blockade of all Iranian ports effective tomorrow at 20:00 GMT, according to the U.S. Naval Forces claim reported by Shargh Daily. (Source: @SharghDaily/171721)

President Trump announced the U.S. will manage the Strait of Hormuz as 'Guardian of Hormuz,' allowing free passage for all nations except Iranian vessels or Iranian clients, and imposing a 20% fee on all cargo transiting the strait to cover security costs, with immediate implementation. (Source: @lelotsenzura/93547, @inon_yttach/9425, @asafroz/51378)

Houthi forces in Yemen launched ballistic missiles at Saudi Arabia, with initial reports of an attack on Abha International Airport; Saudi air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile threat, and Saudi-affiliated mercenaries ordered the closure of all airports to air traffic indefinitely fearing further Houthi retaliation. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/4929, @naya_foriraq/82782, @naya_foriraq/82753, @yediotnews25/132620)
Saudi media reported an additional missile barrage from Yemen toward targets in the kingdom. (Source: @yediotnews25/132620)

sections.threat_assessment: The direct U.S.-Iran military confrontation has entered a new phase with the introduction of unmanned suicide vessels and a declared maritime blockade, significantly raising the risk of miscalculation in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's missile launches from Bandar Abbas demonstrate a willingness to retaliate despite U.S. superiority, while the Houthis' expanded targeting of Saudi Arabia adds a second front that could draw in Gulf states. Israel's continued operations in Gaza and Lebanon, though currently separate, risk convergence if Iranian proxies are activated. The closure of Hormozgan's civil infrastructure indicates Iranian domestic strain, potentially lowering the threshold for asymmetric responses.
sections.regional_response: Saudi Arabia has activated air defenses and preemptively closed its airspace, signaling high alert against Houthi escalation. The UAE's diplomatic involvement in FIFA disciplinary matters suggests continued normalization efforts despite regional turbulence. Gulf states are likely coordinating quietly with U.S. Central Command on maritime security, but public statements remain restrained. Iran's denial of explosions in Bandar Abbas reflects an information control strategy to manage domestic perception while signaling resolve through missile launches. The Trump administration's 'Guardian of Hormuz' declaration with a 20% fee represents a unilateral reshaping of maritime governance that will test international law and allied consensus.
sections.intelligence_notes: The first operational use of maritime one-way attack drones by CENTCOM marks a doctrinal shift toward low-cost, high-volume naval strike capabilities that could proliferate. Iran's missile launches from a fixed base (Chamran) under active U.S. surveillance suggest either degraded command-and-control or a deliberate signaling posture. The IDF's public detailing of Givati Brigade operations deep in Lebanon (Litani, Bint Jbeil, Beaufort) serves both domestic morale and deterrence messaging to Hezbollah. Houthi targeting of Abha International Airport indicates improved intelligence or guidance capabilities, possibly linked to Iranian technical support. The simultaneous domestic political crisis in Israel over draft legislation may affect reserve mobilization readiness if the U.S.-Iran conflict expands.
